summary.text: Amanda Nedweski is a Republican member of the Wisconsin State Assembly from District 32 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Democrat Greg Miller.
She is a former business intelligence consultant who previously served on the Kenosha Unified School District board.

paragraphs.text: Amanda Nedweski was born in Kenosha, Wisconsin, graduated from Mary D. Bradford High School in 1994 and earned a B.A. in communications from the University of Wisconsin-Parkside in 1998.
Her career experience includes working as a senior technology consultant at Braun Consulting, a senior financial analyst at CNH Global and a self-employed business intelligence systems consultant.
Nedweski served on the Kenosha Unified School District school board and was elected to represent District 16 of the Kenosha County Board of Supervisors.
She won the 2022 general election for Assembly District 61, defeating Max Winkels, and the 2024 general election for District 32, defeating Michael Dhindsa.
For 2025-2026 she chairs the Government Accountability and Oversight Committee, is vice-chair of the Colleges and Universities Committee and sits on the Rules Committee.
